new_statements.rule_in_words: Mboko, like all seven C20 (Mbosi-group) languages Ndinga Oba surveys, is a tone language with two level tones (H, L) and two contour tones; tone is lexical/grammatical (e.g. noun-class prefixes are low-toned in some classes and high-toned in others).
new_statements.domain_note: Group-level statement about the whole C20 group (mboko, akwa, ngare, koyo, mbosi, likuba, likwala) in the typological conclusion, not a Mboko-specific phonology page; the Mboko-specific phonology chapter is in Tome 1, which could not be opened (Google Books partial preview could not be reached by automated download).
new_statements.identity_note: Mboko = Guthrie C21 (Ndinga Oba: 'le mboko appelé aussi mboyo.. classé en C21'); Ngare (C23, Glottolog treats as a Mboko dialect; Ndinga Oba treats it as a separate C20 language). The tone statement quoted is Ndinga Oba's group-level typological conclusion for all seven C20 languages (mboko, akwa, ngare, koyo, mbosi, likuba, likwala), not a Mboko-only page. Not to be confused with Wumboko/Mboko of Cameroon (A20, 'Bubia') that surfaces in ASJP sources.

Nothing on stress; lists refs Opombo 2018, Ndinga Oba 1995, Ndamba 1987, Bruner 1908 (wordlist), Kouarata 2014, Grollemund et al. 2015, Ethnologue 2025; alternate names Mboxo, Mbuku; C.21 (Ngare C.23 as dialect).
No mention of tone or stress; Guthrie C.21 (C.23 Ngare), ~27,000 speakers (Ethnologue 2000), Makoua district.
